summary.text: A 30-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes since the age of 6 and non-proliferative retinopathy since 2011 was in her second, unplanned pregnancy. A first pregnancy in 2019 ended in a dystocic birth at 37 weeks. She was treated with MDI insulin and monitored with SMBG and isCGM, and her A1C prior to conception was 6.7%.

She was referred at 13 weeks, and first-trimester isCGM readings were recorded. At 15 weeks therapy was switched to the InPen with the Guardian 4 CGM system, and the insulin carbohydrate ratio was later reduced for more bolus insulin after higher insulin requirements. At 30 weeks time in range was over 89% without severe hypoglycaemia.

She delivered a male infant at 38 weeks, large for gestational age without congenital malformations, who needed temporary monitoring for hyperbilirubinemia that resolved with phototherapy. At 4 weeks postpartum the infant was healthy and the mother had maintained stable glycaemic control.

summary.text: A 36-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes since 2003 and Hashimoto’s thyroiditis since 2010 presented at 8 weeks of an unplanned pregnancy in January 2024. She was on MDI insulin with an intermittently scanned glucose meter, had no knowledge of carbohydrate counting, and had a pre-conception HbA1c of 6.8%.

First-trimester isCGM readings were recorded, and at 10 weeks therapy was upgraded to the InPen with the Guardian 4 CGM system using fixed doses because she could not apply carbohydrate counting. The dose calculator helped adjust meal insulin, and at 28 and 37 weeks time in range was over 84% and 90%.

She delivered a female infant at 39 + 1 weeks weighing 3480 g, appropriate for gestational age and without perinatal complications. Gestational weight gain at the end of pregnancy was 10.5 kg, and a total daily insulin dose of 29.7 units (15.6 units rapid insulin and 14.1 units glargine) was reported.

summary.text: A 34-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes since the age of 14 and a low level of disease knowledge was seen at 8 weeks of an unplanned pregnancy. She was on MDI insulin with an isCGM sensor, had always refused pump therapy, and had a pre-pregnancy HbA1c of 7.3%. Glulisine was immediately switched to insulin lispro.

Switching to the InPen was recommended, with a fixed-dose calculator because she could not apply carbohydrate counting. Low compliance limited sensor use in the second trimester, and ps-TIR rose to 76% in the third trimester with a rising need for rapid-acting insulin and dietician counselling.

At 37 weeks she was admitted for polyhydramnios and delivered a male infant by caesarean section, weighing 3680 g and large for gestational age. At 4 weeks postpartum the mother had stable glycaemic control.
